title: Which digits make a sum of two decimals closest to ten point five?
description: Digits from zero to nine are placed in the boxes of two decimals by planning the carries from the right, the same way as the example in the book, so the sum is exactly 10.5.
teaching_notes: One idea: decide what each place must total, then choose digit pairs. Watch for children who try digits at random.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q15
video_script.why: The child has added decimals place by place with carries and now plans the digits so that a sum reaches a target.
video_script.substitution: Work from the right, decide what each place must total with its carry, then pick digits in pairs.
video_script.anchor: Two empty decimals, each with one box before the point and three boxes after it, and the target 10.5.
video_script.payoff_line: Plan the carries from the right, then choose the digits in pairs

final_answer.spoken: zero point six four three plus nine point eight five seven is exactly ten point five zero zero

maths_rules: hundredths: digits + 1 = 10, so digits total 9: write 0, carry 1
tenths: digits + 1 = 15, so digits total 14: write 5, carry 1
pairs 3 and 7, 4 and 5, 6 and 8, 0 and 9; eight different digits
check: thousandths 3 + 7 = 10, hundredths 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, tenths 6 + 8 + 1 = 15, units 0 + 9 + 1 = 10, sum 10.500
video_script.design: The eight boxes stay on screen. Each place gets a pair of digits, and the carries travel up in one colour.
open_questions: The figure with the boxes is missing from the extracted book text. The layout of one digit before the point and three after it, in each decimal, is taken from the worklist.
